newsitem.title: POLAND: KUEHBACHER SAYS EMU 3 PCT DEFICIT AIM SHOULD STAND.
newsitem.headline: KUEHBACHER SAYS EMU 3 PCT DEFICIT AIM SHOULD STAND.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said in Warsaw on Wednesday that EU member governments should stick to the original 3.0 percent deficit target for European Monetary Union.

"If the governments have agreed on this line, they should not ease it...I have to say 3.0," Kuehbacher told reporters at a banking conference in Warsaw after being asked if there was any leeway in the targets.
Kuehbacher said that once political discussion began on relaxing the target, it would be very difficult to set a new limit.
"Where is the border for discussion? Is it 3.2 percent, is it 3.6 percent or four percent?" he said.

Earlier another Bundesbank council member, Ernst Welteke, said in Vienna that the 3.0 percent target was not written in stone and sustained budget deficits were more important. -- Tomasz Janowski +48 22 653 9700
